leading_positions.synthesis: Three members prefer topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect with an identical trio, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. They share the view that the theory-to-experiment chain (Z2 classification, then HgTe edge transport) is traceable, that about fifteen years of independent confirmation have stabilised the interpretation, and that recognition is overdue rather than premature. Eriksson moved to B040 from B038 after reading the opening ballots and Olsson moved from an earlier trio to this one. They also share the same unresolved weakness: the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Hasan's 3D spectroscopy lie outside the three names, and S.-C. Zhang is deceased. They differ only in emphasis on how serious this is and on the alternatives (Eriksson B038 and B045, Mehlig B028 and B038, Olsson B045 and B016). Citation wording differs slightly across the three files.

Three members prefer the optical lattice clock with the same two names, Katori and Ye. They share the case of independent reproduction in several national laboratories, a clean two-person credit, and a measurement capability at the 1e-18 level that supports tests of relativity, constants and geodesy. They also all name the same reservation, distinctness from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, and the same omitted contributors (Lemonde and SYRTE, Takamoto, Hall-type laser stabilisation). They differ on what the citation should stress, and on their fallbacks (Johansson and Kroll B026 and B007, Lindroth B008 and B007). Johansson still regards B026 as scientifically stronger and has disclosed a conflict there, so his support for B045 is partly a judgement on timing and robustness.

Two members prefer high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with Halzen and Karle, citing the diffuse flux seen in several independent analysis channels within IceCube and the opening of a new observational window. They share the view that the citation should rest on the diffuse flux, not on the source identifications. They also share the concern that the two-name attribution is contestable (AMANDA, other IceCube leaders, deep-water programmes) and both list B045 as an alternative. Both say they cannot settle the credit split from the supplied text, and neither claims independent confirmation of the source associations yet. The Chair is one of the two supporters.

areas_of_agreement: Every member prefers a single-part prize built on one of three ballots (B016, B040, B045), split three, three and two. No member prefers a multi-part configuration.

B045 is named in seven of eight files: preferred by Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth, and an alternative for Danielsson, Eriksson, Olsson and Pearce. It is the most widely acceptable fallback even though only three members prefer it.
All three leading groups judge their own candidate by the same tests: independent confirmation, decisive and traceable contribution, and a clean three-name limit.
The members who prefer B040 and B045 each acknowledge distinctness from an earlier prize as a real argument (2016 topological phases for B040; 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes for B045).
No member reports a recusal-level conflict for their own preferred configuration; the disclosed flags are listed separately.
scientific_disputes: Whether the discovery in B016 is the diffuse flux alone, which the supporters regard as sufficient, or whether source identification (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) must be independently confirmed first, which Danielsson says would make the prize premature.

Whether the optical lattice clock (B045) is a new discovery or an enabling-tool refinement of precision spectroscopy; Danielsson and Johansson note that its largest consequences, such as redefining the second, are still prospective.
Whether topological insulators (B040) are a fresh, distinct discovery or a continuation of the topological-phase theme rewarded in 2016.

Whether a quantum-technology candidate (B026, B007, B028) should be held back after the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize; Johansson regards B026 as the stronger physics, Danielsson wants it delayed.
How much the first-place preference for B016 and B040 (two and three members) should weigh against the broader appearance of B045 as an alternative across the files.
attribution_disputes: B016: whether Halzen and Karle are the right two names given AMANDA, other IceCube leaders and analysis leads, and the deep-water efforts (Baikal, ANTARES, KM3NeT). Danielsson and Pearce both raise this and neither can settle it from the supplied text.

B040: the three-name cap forces a choice among Mele, Hasan and the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Eriksson, Mehlig and Olsson prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp, which omits Hasan's 3D spectroscopy and the HgTe proposal; Zhang is deceased. Mehlig and Olsson ask whether a different split is fairer.

B045: Katori and Ye are common to all supporters, but Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson note Lemonde, Takamoto, the SYRTE group and Hall-type laser stabilisation as contributions outside the pair, and Katori's priority for the magic-wavelength concept needs checking.

Similar proposals differ in laureates and citation: B040 opening ballots differed in the trio and Hasan's omission is contested, B016 has Halzen and Karle against a wider IceCube leadership, and B045 citations differ in whether to stress the 1e-18 accuracy, the many-atom method or the invention.
maturity_disputes: B040 supporters call recognition overdue (about fifteen years of confirmation); the counter-argument is the 2016 prize.
B016: the diffuse flux is established in several channels, but the source picture rests largely on one experiment and awaits confirmation by KM3NeT or Baikal-GVD.
B045: the physics and reproduction are mature, but the redefinition of the second has not happened; members differ on whether waiting would strengthen or merely delay the case.
B038 (twisted bilayer graphene) is called premature by Eriksson because of the unresolved pairing mechanism and its age of about eight years, and Eriksson has moved off it as a first choice.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson (director of WACQT, theorist in superconducting circuits at Chalmers) says he should recuse himself from deciding B026 and probably B008; this does not touch his preferred B045.

Kroll disclosed a mild connection: a PhD-era year in John Hall's laboratory, with Hall's work connected to Ye's group at JILA, and not a direct tie to Katori or Ye. He also notes overlap between his rare-earth quantum-memory work and WACQT and the quantum-information ballots (B007, B026, B028).
Pearce (Chair) discloses a taste bias toward detector-driven astroparticle results and no known tie to the IceCube names, and would recuse if a collaboration link emerged.
Olsson and Mehlig note Chalmers or Gothenburg proximity to Johansson, with no tie to their preferred ballot. Danielsson, Eriksson and Lindroth report no specific conflict.
questions_for_round2: For B016: does the committee cite only the diffuse flux, and can the historical record (AMANDA-era leaders, the IceCube discovery analyses) support Halzen and Karle as the two names?

For B040: if three names are the limit, which third name should join Kane and Molenkamp or replace Mele, or is a 2D versus 3D split fairer, and how should the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and Zhang's death be handled?
For B045: what is the specific new contribution relative to the 2005 and 2012 prizes, and does the committee need the redefinition of the second to appear in the citation or the timing?
Is the committee willing to treat B045 as the consensus candidate if the first-place camps for B016 and B040 cannot resolve their attribution problems, and if not, what would have to change in each?
Does the 2025 superconducting-circuits prize rule out B026 and the other quantum-technology ballots for 2026, or is it only a timing consideration, given Johansson's disclosed flag?

Should any member who changed position after reading the opening ballots (Eriksson, Johansson, Olsson, Lindroth) say which specific argument moved them, so that round 2 tests that argument and not the ranking count?
summary.chair_observation: The committee is split three ways with no majority: three for B040, three for B045 and two for B016, each with a stated attribution or novelty problem that is not yet resolved from the supplied text. B045 has the cleanest credit and is a frequent alternative, B040 has the strongest conceptual argument but the hardest attribution, and B016 has a clear discovery but contested names. As Chair I am a supporter of B016, and I note that when summarising.
